In (2021) 12 SCC 550 (Pramila Vs., State of UP) Hon'ble Supreme Court held that "evidence of a child witness alone can form the basis for conviction and mere absence of any corroborative evidence cannot alone discredit a child witness.

However, where a child witness is to be considered, and more so when he is the sole witness, a heightened level of scrutiny is called for of the evidence so that the court is satisfied with regard to the reliability and genuineness of the evidence of child witness.
In case of tutoring the Court can reject his statement partly or fully.
And inference as to whether child has been tutored or not can be drawn from the contents of its deposition.

Court has to satisfy itself that all possibilities of tutoring or otherwise or ruled out and what was deposed was nothing but the truth".
In (1976) 1 SCC 37(Muluwa S/o Binda and Ors. Vs., State of MP) It was held that "the evidence of an infirm witness does not become reliable merely because it has been corroborated by a number of witness of the same brand "for evidence is to be weighted and not counted".

25.In 1999
Supreme (Guj) 343 (Indrasing M Rao Vs., State) Hon'ble Gujarat High Court held that The meaning of cruelty is given vide explanation to Sec..498A.
It means willful conduct of such nature, as is likely propel, or goad or compel the women to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb of health.

If the women is subjected to harassment with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand, for property or valuable security or coercing and her relative owing to failure on her or her relatives part to meet such demand, the same would also amount to cruelty.
The expression cruelty means and implies harsh and harmful conduct of certain intensity and persistence.

It, therefore covers the acts causing both physical and mental agony and torture, or tyranny and harm as well as unending accusations and recrimination reflecting bitterness putting the victim S.C.No.145/2018 thereof to intense miseries and owes strong stirring up her feeling that life is now not worth living and she should die, being the only option left.
The provision of Sec.498A therefore envisages intention to drag or force the women to commit suicide by unabetted, persistent and grave cruelty.

The meaning of word harass which can be found from the dictionary is to subject some one to unbearable, continuous or repeated or persistent unprovoked vexatious attacks, questions, demands or persecutions or brutality, or tyranny or harm or pain or afflictions, or other unpleasantness, or grave annoyances or troubles.
In short what can be said is that Sec.498A will not come in to play in every case of harassment and/ or cruelty.
Reasonable nexus between cruelty and suicide must be established.

It should therefore be shown that the incessant harassment or cruelty was with a view to force the wife to end her life or fulfill illegal demands of her husband or in laws, and was not matrimonial cruelty namely usual wear and tear of matrimonial life.
It should be hardly stated that the prosecution has to establish the charge beyond reasonable doubt.

No doubt arithmetical accuracy is not expected from the prosecution, but it has to adduce such evidence which would be credible leaving no room to any reasonable doubt"and pointing to the guilt of the accused".
S.C.No.145/2018 In (2020)15 SCC 359 (Rajesh Vs., State of Haryana) Hon'ble Supreme Court held that one incident of slapping of deceased by appellant not proximate to commission of suicide by deceased cannot be a sole ground to hold him responsible for instigating deceased to commit suicide within the meaning of Sec. 306 and 107 of IPC.

literally means to provoke, incite, urge on or bring about by persuasion to do anything.
In cases of alleged abetment of suicide, there must be a proof of direct or indirect act/s of incitement to the commission of suicide.

It could hardly be disputed that the question of cause of a suicide,
particularly in the context of an offence of abetment of suicide, remains a vexed one, involving multifaceted and complex attributes of human behavior and responses/reactions.
In the case of accusation for abetment of suicide, the Court would be looking for cogent and convincing proof of the act/s of incitement to the commission of suicide.

In the case of suicide, mere allegation of harassment of the deceased by another person would not suffice unless there be such action on the part of the accused which compels the person to commit suicide; and such an offending action ought to be proximate to the time of occurrence.
Whether a person has abetted in the commission of suicide by another or not, could only be gathered from the facts and circumstances of each case.

None of the prosecution witnesses supported the case of the prosecution regarding the alleged mental and physical S.C.No.145/2018 harassment meted out by the deceased-Smt.Lakshmamma,
soon before her death.
There is no evidence on record to establish that the accused herein abetted her to commit suicide.
The suicidal death of the deceased-Smt. Lakshmamma itself is not sufficient to establish abetment to commit suicide as discussed in the decisions referred above.
27.The alleged harassment of physical and mental cruelty meted out by the deceased, and offence of abetment committed by the accused has not been established by the prosecution.
In AIR 2010 Supreme Court 327 (Gangula Mohan Reddy Vs., State of Andhra Pradesh) it was held that "Mens rea and active act by the accused is essential to constitute offence punishable U/s.306 of IPC.

28. The deceased-Smt.Lakshmamma and accused are being the husband and wife, and they had trivial issue with regard to matrimonial dispute, that itself is not a ground to believe that the accused has abetted the deceased to commit suicide.

The expression cruelty means and implies harsh and harmful conduct of certain intensity and persistence.
It, therefore covers the acts causing both physical and mental agony and torture, or tyranny and harm as well as unending accusations and recrimination reflecting bitterness putting the victim S.C.No.145/2018 thereof to intense miseries and owes strong stirring up her feeling that life is now not worth living and she should die, being the only option left.
The provision of Sec.498A therefore envisages intention to drag or force the women to commit suicide by unabetted, persistent and grave cruelty.
The meaning of word harass which can be found from the dictionary is to subject some one to unbearable, continuous or repeated or persistent unprovoked vexatious attacks, questions, demands or persecutions or brutality, or tyranny or harm or pain or afflictions, or other unpleasantness, or grave annoyances or troubles.
In short what can be said is that Sec.498A will not come in to play in every case of harassment and/ or cruelty.
Reasonable nexus between cruelty and suicide must be established.
It should therefore be shown that the incessant harassment or cruelty was with a view to force the wife to end her life or fulfill illegal demands of her husband or in laws, and was not matrimonial cruelty namely usual wear and tear of matrimonial life.
